clue.text: Yankee sniffs second shot of Michter's and verifies round

indicators.note: a shot is a small first taste of a drink, so only the opening letter of the whiskey's name is taken
the word for verifies goes around the single letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
checks means verifies
first letter of the whiskey brand

explanation.surface: An American noses a bourbon from the Michter's distillery and approves the round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Michter's is an American whiskey. 'Yankee' marks the answer as US slang, from Yiddish: to schmeck is to smell or taste.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang, borrowed from Yiddish, schmeck means to smell or taste, so the third-person form matches the verb sniffs.

clue.text: A land unit's lost reputed good character

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so the single letter named before it disappears from the measure

blocks.note: an acre is a measure of land area
dit is a French-derived word in Chambers meaning named or reputed

explanation.surface: A military unit has lost its supposed reputation for good conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A land unit' reads like an army unit, but it is the acre with its A lost. DIT is an obscure Chambers word, as in a stage name 'dit' something.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit means good reputation or standing, as in 'a person of credit', the sense of good character.

clue.text: Ran into crew members mining rare bones

indicators.note: mining means digging into, so the sailors are set inside the word for excellent

blocks.note: met means encountered, ran into
rare can mean excellent; A1 means first-rate, written with I for 1
tars are sailors

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled on a ship's crew digging up unusual bones.
explanation.walkthrough: Rare in its old sense means splendid or excellent, matching A1, here AI.
explanation.definitionFit: The metatarsi are the five long bones of the foot between ankle and toes, so they are bones.

clue.text: Ladies who sing refrains trading gold for advance payment

indicators.note: trading one thing for another means exchanging them, so one piece is swapped out and another put in its place

blocks.note: choruses are the repeated parts of a song
or is gold in heraldry
an ante is a stake put up in advance, as in poker

explanation.surface: Singers who give up their gold records in exchange for money up front.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanteuse is a female singer, especially in a nightclub or cabaret, so the plural means women who sing.

clue.text: Year wasted by so very complex mechanical system

indicators.note: wasted means lost or squandered, so the letter for year is lost by the phrase that follows
complex means intricate or tangled, so the remaining letters are tangled into a new order

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for year
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a whole year was squandered on an overcomplicated piece of machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A servo, short for servomechanism, is an automatic device that controls a larger mechanism, so it is a mechanical system.

clue.text: Oxygen escaping from substandard plane

indicators.note: something escaping leaves, so the gas symbol drops out of the words that follow

blocks.note: chemical symbol for oxygen
of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'
light means short of the proper weight, so below standard

explanation.surface: A warning that a badly built aircraft is leaking its oxygen supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escaping from' looks like one phrase, but 'from' is itself wordplay: OF + LIGHT, then the O escapes, leaving F + LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is an aircraft making a scheduled journey, as in 'the flight landed late', so it can stand for a plane.

clue.text: Launch force with anger …

blocks.note: F is the physics symbol for force
ire is anger

explanation.surface: An order to propel something violently while in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into the next one, which uses this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire a missile or rocket is to launch it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: … out of which you may draw no reason

indicators.note: to draw something out of a container is to remove it, so those letters come out of the word

blocks.note: which refers back to the previous clue's answer, fire; a great fire is an inferno
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the fiery outburst: from it you can draw no rational conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis makes 'which' stand for 6 down, FIRE, here as INFERNO; remove NO to get INFER. 'Draw' also hints at the answer's sense of drawing a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning, so the verb reason fits it.

clue.text: Such art is shown off out of salon's door?

definitions.text: Such art is shown off out of salon's door?

indicators.note: a door is the way in, so it stands for the opening letter of the word before it
out of means removed from, so that single letter is taken away from the phrase
off can mean wrong or awry, so the letters are set out in a disordered way

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of salon

explanation.surface: Fresh styles are paraded by customers stepping out of a hairdresser's.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one S from SUCH ART IS and rearrange. The whole clue also describes the answer: newly cut hair is shown off as clients leave the salon.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairdressing is a craft whose results clients display as they leave the salon, so the whole clue paints this answer.

clue.text: Ultimately picked up the pieces? Didn't bother

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the closing letter of each following word is picked out

blocks.note: last letters of up, the, pieces and Didn't

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they tidied up after a breakage, who answers that they didn't bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up the pieces' reads as a set phrase, but 'picked' belongs with 'Ultimately' as the selector; the fodder starts at 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bother is a nuisance, and a pest is likewise an annoying person or thing, both nouns.

clue.text: Roaming craft fair restricting current overhead fluctuations?

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters wander into a new order
restricting means hemming in, so the rearranged letters hold the electrical symbol inside them

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A visitor wandering round a craft fair that caps the flow of electricity to its stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' tempts AC or DC, but here it is the single letter I, the symbol used in physics formulas.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft passing above vary in number through the day, so air traffic is a playful description of things fluctuating overhead, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Speaking for PA: sorry, I can't do it

indicators.note: sorry can mean in a poor or wretched state, so the words that follow are in a mess

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A secretary, asked to take down the boss's words, apologises that the task is beyond them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictation is speech delivered for a personal assistant (PA) to write down, so it is speaking done for the PA.

clue.text: End of trip on which train crew periodically charge

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that closing letter is kept
periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter of the following words is used

blocks.note: final letter of trip
second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of train crew

explanation.surface: At the end of a journey, the railway staff now and then demand a fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On which' puts the single letter first, with the alternate letters following it in the across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A price is the amount asked for something, just as a charge is the sum demanded for goods or a service.

clue.text: Thesaurus, could it be, supporting poet's first choice?

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter only of the writer's word
in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath, so the book word comes after the letter

blocks.note: first letter of poet
a thesaurus is an example of a reference book; 'could it be' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a thesaurus could back up a poet's favourite word.
explanation.definitionFit: A preference is the thing one favours over others, so it means a choice.

clue.text: Terrain reduced to powder

blocks.note: first meaning: land, the surface of the earth
second meaning: past participle of grind, crushed fine

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests land pulverised into dust; the two halves are separate meanings, a noun and a past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for the land underfoot and also the past participle of grind, describing something crushed into fine particles.

clue.text: Chap from Cardiff maybe spotted item in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a die, one of a pair of dice, is covered in spots

explanation.surface: A Welshman catches sight of something at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'seen' but describes a dotted object. Dai is a common Welsh man's name, Cardiff being the Welsh capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Dai is a typical Welsh first name, short for David, so a man from Cardiff might be called that.

clue.text: Touching banking counter for my money? Withdrawn!

indicators.note: counter means running in the opposite direction, so the phrase is read backwards
banking means forming a bank on either side, so the word for touching flanks the turned phrase

blocks.note: re means concerning or touching on
for my money means in my opinion, that is, to me

explanation.surface: Someone at a bank counter is told their cash has been withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The banking scene is a decoy: 'banking' and 'counter' are both instructions, and 'for my money' is the idiom meaning 'to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote person is aloof and reserved, which is what withdrawn means when describing someone's manner.

clue.text: Order Wham!'s hit – it's out, tosh

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters are arranged afresh
read as 'it is', this says two letters of the song word are to be replaced by the next word

blocks.note: the pop duo's name with its S
taken as written
taken as written, replacing two letters of the previous word

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a new single by the 1980s pop duo Wham!: it's released, and it's rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'hit – it's out' as HIT with its IT becoming OUT, giving HOUT; rearrange with WHAMS. Mouthwash is slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouthwash is informal British slang for nonsense or empty talk, the same meaning as tosh.

clue.text: Nutty vicar and pop share cell that contains a hundred rodents

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so the clergyman's title goes haywire into a new order
sharing a cell means occupying one space together, so the overlapping letter is written once and the duplicate is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
pop is a fizzy drink such as cola
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A dotty clergyman and his father are locked up together in a cell overrun with rats.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged vicar ends in C and the drink begins with C, so the two words overlap on that one letter, the hundred the shared cell contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Arvicola is the zoological genus of water voles, which are rodents, so it can be defined by them.

clue.text: Emile's vineyard is culmination of wine holiday

indicators.note: the culmination is the very end, so only the last letter of the drink word is used

blocks.note: cru is French for a vineyard or its growth; Emile is a French name
taken as written
final letter of wine

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's vineyard visit is the high point of a wine-tasting trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Emile's signals that the vineyard is to be given in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a pleasure voyage taken as a vacation, so it is a kind of holiday.

clue.text: Rush entering US League, then United let in nine!

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the sports league goes inside the number
let in means admitted, so the number holds what precedes it within

blocks.note: the National Football League of America
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names
Roman numeral for nine

explanation.surface: A football report: a team rushing into the American league, then Manchester United conceding nine goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let in nine' reads as a heavy defeat, but it means the Roman numeral takes the other letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An influx is a sudden arrival of people or things in large numbers, which a rush describes.

clue.text: This follows immediately, without a forward space, for general use

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the punctuation word goes without its single letter

blocks.note: in the clue itself, the mark straight after 'immediately' is a comma
taken as written
on means forward, as in 'go on'

explanation.surface: An instruction about typing: a word follows directly, with no space before it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: 'This' is the punctuation mark that does follow 'immediately'. 'Space' looks like typesetting jargon but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A common is a piece of open land that everyone in a community may use, so it is a space for general use.

clue.text: Heard about place one's assigned to new arrival

indicators.note: heard about means reported by ear, so the sound of a word matters rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a berth is a bunk or mooring allotted to someone

explanation.surface: Someone learns the spot they have been allocated, ready for a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound identical; the spelling with I is the one meaning childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: A birth is the arrival of a baby into the world, so the event can be clued as a new arrival.

clue.text: Reversing broke a sword guard

indicators.note: reversing means turning backwards, so the word for broke is read from its end

blocks.note: bust means broke, as in going bankrupt
taken as written

explanation.surface: Driving backwards smashed a protective guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' looks like a verb in the past tense here, but it is the adjective meaning penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsuba is the metal guard between blade and hilt on a Japanese sword, so it is a sword guard.

clue.text: A surprise, that is, about Green Line deposition

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the exclamation goes around the colour word

blocks.note: an exclamation of surprise
vert is green in heraldry
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A surprising upset about the Green Line bus route, a London service.
explanation.walkthrough: Green Line is a real London bus company, so the capitals make the two words look like one name.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposition is the removal of a ruler from power, and an overthrow is exactly that kind of forced removal.

clue.text: Old fault muffles speaker

indicators.note: to muffle is to wrap something up, so the word for fault wraps around the letter

blocks.note: a vice is a failing or flaw
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old technical fault deadens the sound coming from a loudspeaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests audio equipment, but it means a person speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice can mean a person who speaks for a view, as in 'a lone voice', so it stands for a speaker.

clue.text: Labour's reward, with time

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Workers, or the Labour Party, being paid back over time.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital L hints at the political party, but it is plain work.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage is the regular payment earned for work done, so it is the reward for labour.

clue.text: Samples taken from this Paul scattered in magical brew

indicators.note: scattered means thrown about, so the name's letters land in a new order
in places the jumbled name inside the word for a magical brew

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a potion is a magic drink

explanation.surface: A wizard called Paul is mixed into a cauldron's brew, from which tasters draw samples.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics, samples are drawn from a population, the whole group under study.

clue.text: Conflict church dispelled from entrances

indicators.note: dispelled means driven away, so the abbreviation is removed from the word that follows

blocks.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church
the verb: entrances means bewitches or charms

explanation.surface: A dispute in which the church banishes something from its doorways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrances' looks like a noun for doorways, but it is the verb meaning enchants.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms means warfare or fighting, as in 'a call to arms', which makes it a word for armed conflict.

clue.text: Like a cracked back injury?

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the whole string of letters is read from the end

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, like
taken as written
cracked means crazy

explanation.surface: A doctor asks whether the patient's back injury feels like a crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked back' sounds like a medical complaint; 'cracked' means crazy and 'back' is the reversal instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is harm done to a body or object, so it serves as a general word for an injury.

clue.text: Exotic polyurethanes making this kind of seal – yours?

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the long word's letters are made unfamiliar by rearrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written: these letters are the other half of the mix

explanation.surface: Fancy plastics used to make a seal, asking which kind is yours.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the answer plus YOURS rearranges into POLYURETHANES, so take those five letters away and shuffle the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The elephant seal is a huge marine mammal named for the male's trunk-like nose, so the answer names a kind of seal.
